topics.label: algorithm / computation
excellence: the chosen approach with its time AND space complexity, and why that fits the input size
the invariant maintained at each step, stated explicitly
the edge cases enumerated with expected behaviour: empty, single, maximum, overflow / precision, duplicates, negatives
determinism stated (or where randomness enters and how it is seeded)
a correctness argument and a concrete test oracle: a property, a round-trip, or a brute-force check on small inputs
the common naive approach named and why it is rejected (the trap a generalist falls into)
pitfalls: unstated complexity, or a hidden quadratic / repeated work
off-by-one or boundary handling at the ends of the range
integer overflow, float precision, or unit / coordinate confusion
empty / null / single-element input not handled
non-determinism that breaks reproducibility
no oracle - no way to know it is correct

topics.label: analytics / analysis
excellence: the decision the analysis serves, and the question stated precisely
the RIGHT metric chosen (and why), with vanity metrics and wrong denominators rejected
data caveats stated up front: sampling, bias, missing data, the time period
correlation-vs-causation discipline, and the confounders named
segmentation that survives Simpson's paradox - the aggregate AND the segments
statistical rigor where it matters (significance, confidence intervals), not false precision
a clear narrative ending in the action it implies, and a reproducible query / notebook
pitfalls: a vanity metric or the wrong denominator
correlation reported as causation
ignored sampling / survivorship bias
p-hacking or false precision with no significance
an unsegmented aggregate hiding a reversal (Simpson's paradox)
a chart with no decision; a non-reproducible result

topics.label: software architecture
excellence: the real problem and constraints named, and the quality attributes that matter here RANKED (what wins a tie)
the components, their responsibilities, and the boundaries between them
a single owner for each piece of shared state / each cross-cutting concern
the key decisions recorded ADR-style: the choice, the rejected alternatives, and the tradeoff
the failure modes and the detect -> recover -> degrade behaviour for each
an evolution path: how it extends, and what it deliberately does NOT do yet
the SIMPLEST design that meets the constraints - complexity justified, not assumed
pitfalls: a box-and-arrow diagram with no decisions, tradeoffs, or rejected alternatives
gold-plating / speculative generality for needs that do not exist yet
a shared concern (state machine, feedback surface) that no component owns
ignoring the dominant quality attribute (e.g. optimizing flexibility when latency is the point)
no failure story; tight coupling that blocks the likely change
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/architecture.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: backend / API
excellence: an explicit API contract: each endpoint's request shape, response shape, status codes, and one typed error envelope
validation at the boundary and AUTHORIZATION on every path (not just authentication)
idempotency and concurrency handled: what a retry does, what two writers do
stated transaction boundaries and the consistency guarantee (what is atomic, what is eventual)
observability built in: structured logs with a correlation id, key metrics, a health / readiness signal
pagination, limits, and rate limits on anything unbounded or expensive
versioning / backward-compatibility thought through for a contract others depend on
pitfalls: unvalidated input reaching logic or the database; an error path that leaks internals
a route missing authorization, or an IDOR (one user reaching another's id)
a non-idempotent write behind a retry; a race between concurrent writers
an unbounded query, an N+1, or a missing pagination / limit
secrets in logs or code; no rate limit on an expensive path
no observability - a production failure would be invisible
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/backend.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: CLI / tool
excellence: a clear command surface: subcommands, args, flags, and their defaults
an I/O contract: stdin / stdout / stderr, correct exit codes, and a machine-readable (--json) output
actionable help and error messages (what happened + what to do next)
safety for destructive actions: a --dry-run and a confirmation
config + cross-platform assumptions made explicit (paths, shells, env)
composability: quiet / verbose, pipe-friendly output, idempotent re-runs
pitfalls: unclear flags or no --help; a flag that secretly does two things
wrong or missing exit codes (success reported on failure)
noisy, unstructured output that cannot be piped or parsed
a destructive action with no confirm / dry-run
an unhelpful error ('something went wrong') with no next step
a hidden platform assumption (a path separator, a shell builtin)
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/cli.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: data / pipeline
excellence: a defined schema: tables / types, keys, constraints, and the units / timezone / encoding conventions
idempotent, replayable processing - a re-run produces the same result
explicit handling of late, duplicate, out-of-order, and malformed records (a dead-letter path, not a crash)
bounded memory at volume: streaming / chunking instead of load-everything
a migration / backfill story with a forward AND a rollback step
data-quality checks and a surfaced count of what was dropped or quarantined
lineage / observability: where data came from and whether the run was healthy
pitfalls: no dedup / idempotency key - a re-run double-counts
unbounded memory on a large input (load-all instead of stream)
a malformed / missing-field record crashes the run instead of a dead-letter path
schema drift or an implicit type with no validation
timezone / encoding / null-vs-empty pitfalls
no migration plan, or one with no rollback
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/data.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: debugging / diagnosis
excellence: a reliable, minimal reproduction established FIRST
the actual ROOT cause found - not the symptom - with an evidence chain that proves it
each hypothesis tested against an observation, not assumed
the blast radius mapped: what else is affected by the same cause
a fix that addresses the cause, with why it does
a regression test that FAILS before the fix and passes after
prevention: how this class of bug is kept from recurring
pitfalls: fixing the symptom while the cause survives
no reliable reproduction - debugging by guess
guess-and-check with no hypothesis; stacking workarounds
no regression test to prove the fix and prevent relapse
ignoring the blast radius (the same cause elsewhere)
a 'fix' that only masks the failure
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/debugging.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: general
excellence: the real goal behind the request named, and what using the result should feel like
the parts and how they connect into one whole
the edge cases and failure modes that actually matter here
what 'good' concretely means for this task, and the load-bearing decisions made to hit it
pitfalls: (carried by the four structural lenses: load-bearing unknowns, unowned seams, vague parts, failure modes)

topics.label: infrastructure / devops
excellence: reproducible and declarative: infrastructure as code, pinned versions, no snowflake steps
an explicit deploy path AND a rollback path
observability: logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and the SLOs they defend
secrets managed (a vault / secret store), never in plaintext or committed env
least-privilege IAM and stated network boundaries
disaster recovery: backups, and a restore that has actually been tested
cost awareness: the cost driver named and bounded
pitfalls: manual / snowflake setup that cannot be reproduced
no rollback path; no tested restore
no observability or alerting - an outage is noticed by users first
secrets in plaintext, env files, or the repo
over-broad IAM permissions; an open network boundary
unpinned versions; an unbounded cost driver

topics.label: performance
excellence: a goal with a budget: the latency / throughput target, stated at p50 AND p99
measure first - profile and name the ACTUAL bottleneck, never optimize on a guess
the dominant cost identified, and the optimization aimed squarely at it
the optimization's tradeoff stated (memory for speed, clarity for cycles) and accepted deliberately
caching / batching / parallelism applied only where it pays, with a cache-invalidation story
a benchmark that guards against regression, and a stated 'good enough' stopping point
pitfalls: optimizing without measuring; a guessed bottleneck
micro-optimizing code that is not on the hot path
a cache with no invalidation or staleness story
premature / over-optimization that destroys clarity for no real gain
no benchmark or regression guard
ignoring the p99 / tail latency
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/performance.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: refactor
excellence: behaviour preserved - a characterization / regression test net stood up BEFORE touching code
one clear motivation: the smell, coupling, or duplication being removed
small, reversible steps, each one green
the seams and boundaries genuinely improved, not just moved
strict scope: no behaviour change smuggled in under the refactor
a measurable improvement (complexity, coupling, readability) and the risk + rollback stated
pitfalls: changing behaviour under cover of a refactor
no test net - behaviour preservation cannot be proven
one giant non-reversible step
scope creep beyond the stated motivation
refactoring with no motivation - churn for its own sake
breaking a public contract others depend on
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/refactor.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: research / investigation
excellence: the real question framed precisely, and what a DECISION-USEFUL answer would have to contain
established fact (sourced and dated) separated from inference, separated from opinion
triangulation: at least two independent sources per load-bearing claim, and where they disagree named
the strongest counter-position and the best alternative steel-manned, not just the favored answer
sources weighted by quality (primary / official > secondary > anecdote), and said so
a recommendation with its confidence and the one finding that would change it
the remaining unknowns surfaced, with the cost of resolving each
pitfalls: a load-bearing claim resting on a single source
a stale fact stated as current (no date on a volatile claim)
confirmation bias - only the favored side investigated
citing a summary / blog as if it were the primary source
a wall of findings with no decision or recommendation
hidden assumptions presented as facts
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/research.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: security
excellence: a threat model: the assets, the adversaries, the attack surface, and the trust boundaries
authentication, authorization, and least privilege at every boundary
input validation and output encoding against injection / XSS / deserialization
secrets and key management with rotation, and a fail-CLOSED posture
defense in depth - no single control is the only thing standing
auditability and the abuse cases (not just the happy path)
data protection: encryption at rest and in transit, and PII minimization
pitfalls: no threat model - controls with no stated adversary
authorization gaps / IDOR; trusting client-supplied input
an injection / XSS / deserialization surface
secrets mishandled; a fail-OPEN default
no audit trail; over-broad permissions
PII exposed at rest or in logs
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/security.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: distributed system
excellence: the components and, for each shared state machine, ONE owner and its contract (states, transitions, message shapes)
the failure modes - partition, disconnect, retry storm, slow consumer, split brain - each with detect / recover / degrade
the consistency model stated (strong / eventual / causal) and where it applies
the end-to-end sequence of how the parts work together
backpressure and bounded resources (queues, connections, memory) under load
idempotency and ordering guarantees made explicit
observability of the distributed state - you can tell what every node believes
pitfalls: a shared state machine or feedback surface that no single component owns
an unhandled partial failure: a disconnect, a retry storm, a slow consumer
no consistency story - two components can silently disagree
a single point of failure or an unbounded resource under load
a race or ordering assumption between components
retries with no backpressure or idempotency

topics.label: technical writing
excellence: the reader, their goal, and their prior knowledge identified - and the writing pitched to them
the one thing they must leave with, stated FIRST (the lede is not buried)
the right shape for the job: tutorial vs how-to vs reference vs explanation (not a blur of all four)
concrete, runnable examples - and the snippets actually work
the WHY, not only the what; the reasoning that lets the reader generalize
scannable structure: meaningful headings, lists, short paragraphs
the failure / edge cases and a troubleshooting path, in precise plain language
pitfalls: burying the lede; the reader cannot tell what matters
the wrong document type for the need
no examples, or untested snippets that do not run
curse-of-knowledge gaps - steps obvious to the author, missing for the reader
a wall of prose with no structure; explaining what but never why
stale / unversioned against the thing it documents
topics.source: harden-plan skill packs/technical-writing.md (local managed skill ~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/harden-plan, read 2026-10-07)

topics.label: UI / frontend
excellence: every state of every screen is designed: loading, empty / first-run, error, success, partial, offline
a deliberate visual hierarchy - what the eye hits first, second, third - set by a real type / spacing / colour scale
responsive from small to large viewport, with the layout's reflow stated, not just 'it's responsive'
a feedback language: how the UI answers every action (hover / active / focus, optimistic update, toast, inline)
accessibility as a baseline: keyboard path, focus order, AA contrast, labels, reduced-motion - not a later epic
micro-interactions with concrete timing + easing that make it feel alive, never gratuitous
copy that survives reality: empty, very long, error, and i18n text all have a place
pitfalls: a screen with no empty / loading / error state designed
no keyboard / focus / screen-reader story; colour-only meaning; low contrast
a layout that breaks at some viewport or assumes a fixed pixel width
a flat hierarchy where everything has the same weight
an action with no visible feedback; motion with no stated intent or duration
hardcoded copy with no room for empty / long / localised text
